classification.difficultyReason: Form a one-variable area function using the shared wire-length constraint, classify its stationary point and interpret the two required wire lengths.

content.prompt: A 3 m piece of wire is cut into 2 pieces and bent around to form a square and a circle. Find the size of the 2 lengths, correct to 2 decimal places, that will make the total area of the square and circle a minimum.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ metres be the square's side length and $r$ metres be the circle's radius.

$$\begin{align*}P&=4x+2\pi r\\3&=4x+2\pi r\\r&=\frac{3-4x}{2\pi}\end{align*}$$

Both pieces have positive length, so $0<x<\frac34$.

$$\begin{align*}A&=x^2+\pi r^2\\A&=x^2+\pi\left(\frac{3-4x}{2\pi}\right)^2\\A&=x^2+\frac{(3-4x)^2}{4\pi}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A'(x)&=2x+\frac{8x-6}{\pi}\\0&=2x+\frac{8x-6}{\pi}\\0&=2\pi x+8x-6\\0&=\pi x+4x-3\\3&=\pi x+4x\\x(\pi+4)&=3\\x&=\frac{3}{\pi+4}\end{align*}$$

$$A''(x)=2+\frac8\pi>0.$$

The stationary point lies in the domain and is the global minimum because $A''(x)>0$ throughout the domain.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Square perimeter}&=4\left(\frac3{\pi+4}\right)\\\text{Square perimeter}&=\frac{12}{\pi+4}\\\text{Square perimeter}&\approx1.68\text{ m}\\\text{Circle perimeter}&=3-\frac{12}{\pi+4}\\\text{Circle perimeter}&=\frac{3\pi}{\pi+4}\\\text{Circle perimeter}&\approx1.32\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
